backward_compat_traps.rule: The 16-bit Virtual Link Identifier is carried in the lower 16 bits of the destination MAC (constant 0x03:00:00:00 + VL ID); switches forward on VL ID, not on learned MACs.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Treating AFDX like learning/spanning-tree Ethernet is wrong — forwarding is static, VL-ID based.
Arbitrary inter-frame intervals are not allowed; the BAG must be a power of two in 1..128 ms.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Sub-VLs round-robin into the parent VL shaper and share its BAG; they do not appear on the wire.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Assuming each Sub-VL has its own BAG over-allocates bandwidth.

backward_compat_traps.rule: The redundancy Sequence Number is 1 byte, range 1..255 (0 reserved for reset/first frame).
backward_compat_traps.trap: Using a wider SN or wrapping through 0 breaks Integrity Checking / Redundancy Management.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Both networks carry every frame; the receiver delivers the first valid copy and discards the duplicate.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Expecting retransmission (TCP-style) is wrong — AFDX uses spatial redundancy + UDP, not retransmission.

fields.spec_version: ARINC Specification 664 Part 7 — Aircraft Data Network, Part 7: Avionics Full-Duplex Switched Ethernet (AFDX) Network
previous_versions: IEEE Std 802.3-1985 (original 10BASE5 Thick Ethernet — DEC + Intel + Xerox 'DIX Ethernet II' commercial precursor 1980)
IEEE Std 802.3i-1990 (10BASE-T over twisted pair — birth of the structured wiring + hub topology)
IEEE Std 802.3u-1995 (Fast Ethernet — 100BASE-T family: 100BASE-TX, 100BASE-T4, 100BASE-FX, introduced MII Clause 22 + AutoNeg Clause 28)
IEEE Std 802.3x-1997 (Full-duplex + PAUSE-frame flow control — MAC Control sublayer Clause 31)
IEEE Std 802.3ab-1999 (1000BASE-T gigabit copper over Cat 5e UTP — Clause 40)
IEEE Std 802.3ac-1998 (4-byte VLAN tag — increased max frame size to 1522 B; tags integrated with 802.1Q)
IEEE Std 802.3ad-2000 (Link Aggregation — later moved to IEEE 802.1AX)
IEEE Std 802.3ae-2002 (10 Gigabit Ethernet — 10GBASE-X family + XGMII Clause 46 + Clause 45 MMD addressing)

key_changes.summary: Defines AFDX: deterministic profiled IEEE 802.3 switched Ethernet adding Virtual Links (16-bit VL ID in the dest MAC, Sub-VLs), Bandwidth Allocation Gap (1..128 ms) with bounded jitter and traffic shaping/policing, dual-network (A/B) redundancy with a 1-byte Sequence Number, per-network Integrity Checking and first-valid-wins Redundancy Management, End Systems and AFDX Switches, and UDP/IP over the VL with sampling/queuing ports.

future_versions_industry_outline.summary: 10 Gb/s over 4-pair Cat 6a / Cat 7 UTP using LDPC + DSQ128 modulation; introduces Clause 55 PHY.
Adds Low-Power Idle (LPI) signaling for 100BASE-TX, 1000BASE-T, 10GBASE-T — Clause 78.
Introduces 40 Gb/s and 100 Gb/s over multi-lane fiber (40GBASE-SR4, 100GBASE-LR4, etc.) and Clause 81 XLGMII / CGMII.
100 Gb/s over backplane + twinax with FEC.
Single-pair automotive Ethernet PHYs sharing the same Clause 4 MAC.
Higher per-lane PAM4 rates targeting 800 GbE / 1.6 TbE.

fields.version_naming_history_note: AFDX is the trademarked Airbus implementation of the ARINC 664 Part 7 standard (Aircraft Data Network, Part 7), itself a deterministic profile of IEEE 802.3 Ethernet. It is the avionics backbone of aircraft such as the Airbus A380/A350 and Boeing 787. Facts here are grounded in the ARINC 664 Part 7 specification structure (Virtual Links, BAG, redundancy management, End Systems and switches, UDP/IP).
related_standards: ARINC 664 (Aircraft Data Network) — the multi-part family; Part 7 specifies AFDX.
ARINC 429 (Mark 33 DITS) — the legacy point-to-point avionics bus that AFDX largely supersedes for high-bandwidth data.
